questions.lead: A record of 20,000 flights from 59 US airports in 2001. The flights that left Sacramento (SMF) in March.
questions.ask: How many minutes of lateness did those late flights add up to?

parts.label: Flights
parts.hint: How many of this record's flights left from here that month?

parts.label: Share that landed 15+ minutes late
parts.hint: What percent of them landed 15 or more minutes after schedule?

parts.label: Minutes late, on average
parts.hint: Among the flights that were that late, how many minutes late on average?

questions.fact: 178 flights left, 35 of them (19.7%) landed 15 or more minutes late, and those were late by 38.0 minutes on average: 1,329 minutes in all. Among the 162 other airport-months in this record, nine in ten added up to between 125 and 3,640 minutes.
questions.why: Total lateness is how many flights, times the share that land late, times how late the late ones are. A big airport has many flights and a small one has few, and that one fact swamps the rest. Think of each part on its own, with a range you would bet 19 to 1 on.

questions.lead: A record of 20,000 flights from 59 US airports in 2001. The flights that left Providence (PVD) in January.
questions.ask: How many minutes of lateness did those late flights add up to?

parts.label: Flights
parts.hint: How many of this record's flights left from here that month?

parts.label: Share that landed 15+ minutes late
parts.hint: What percent of them landed 15 or more minutes after schedule?

parts.label: Minutes late, on average
parts.hint: Among the flights that were that late, how many minutes late on average?

questions.fact: 65 flights left, 10 of them (15.4%) landed 15 or more minutes late, and those were late by 31.4 minutes on average: 314 minutes in all. Among the 162 other airport-months in this record, nine in ten added up to between 125 and 3,640 minutes.
questions.why: Total lateness is how many flights, times the share that land late, times how late the late ones are. A big airport has many flights and a small one has few, and that one fact swamps the rest. Think of each part on its own, with a range you would bet 19 to 1 on.

questions.lead: Seattle, the 14 days starting 7 November 2012.
questions.ask: How many mm of rain fell in all?

parts.label: Rainy days
parts.hint: How many of the 14 days have any measurable rain?

parts.label: Rain on a rainy day
parts.hint: On average, how many mm fall on a day that has rain?

questions.fact: 102.4 mm fell: 9 of the 14 days had measurable rain, and a rainy day averaged 11.4 mm. Among the 137 other 14-day stretches within twenty days of the same date of the year (not overlapping this one), nine in ten had between 10.4 and 160.7 mm in all.
questions.why: Rain is two questions, not one: how often does it rain, and how much when it does? You can reason about each (a Seattle winter fortnight is mostly wet; a wet day is usually a few mm, with the odd downpour) far better than you can guess the total. Give each part its own honest range, and let the worksheet combine them.
